clue.text: Complaint of boy in springtime

indicators.note: the word in puts the boy inside the season named next

parts.note: May is a month of springtime
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Someone asks what ailment a young lad caught in the spring.
explanation.definitionFit: A malady is an illness, and a complaint in the medical sense is an ailment.

clue.text: Suspect condensation and corrosion

parts.note: mist is fine water droplets condensed in the air
rust is the corrosion of iron

explanation.surface: Someone eyes damp and rusting metalwork with suspicion.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to doubt or have no faith in them, a verb sense.

clue.text: Sporting official who keeps in touch

definitions.text: Sporting official who keeps in touch

parts.words: Sporting official who keeps in touch
parts.note: reads like a friendly referee who stays in contact, but touch is the area beyond the sideline in rugby and football, which this assistant official watches

explanation.surface: A sports official who stays in contact with people.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby and football, touch is the ground beyond the side lines; the official on that line flags when the ball goes out of play.
explanation.definitionFit: The assistant referee running the touchline signals when the ball crosses out of play.

clue.text: Earthenware drain

definitions.meaning: Delft-style glazed pottery, also spelt this shorter way
an old and dialect word for a ditch or drain dug in the ground

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both glazed Dutch-style pottery and a dug channel for carrying water away.

clue.text: Reported race-medley, using this sound equipment

definitions.text: Reported race-medley, using this sound equipment

parts.words: Reported race-medley, using this sound equipment
parts.note: a medley of sounds, or a race commentary, is captured and played back on a device that stores sound on magnetic strip

explanation.surface: A commentator reports a medley relay race with the help of audio gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that captures sound on magnetic strip is used to keep a report of events.

clue.text: Ditch for keeps?

parts.note: looks like throwing something away permanently, but a keep is a castle's strongest tower, and a water-filled ditch protects it

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to throw something away for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A castle's keep was ringed by a defensive water-filled trench.

clue.text: Exercise only outside and in public

indicators.note: the word only goes outside, so it wraps round the exercise letters

parts.note: taken as written
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone takes exercise only in the open air, for all to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something openly means doing it without concealment, where everyone can see.

clue.text: Fat and aggressive animal

definitions.meaning: a dairy fat spread on bread
a creature that butts with its head, such as a ram or goat

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a dairy spread and, read as one who butts, a head-charging beast.

clue.text: Legs in movement make one run

indicators.note: movement says the letters of the preceding words are shifted about

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: Moving one's legs gets a cricketer one run.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman's one run is a single; 'movement' rearranges LEGS IN.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a lone run scored off a ball is called by this name.

clue.text: Discernible as a quiet Mum, for instance

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
a mother is one example of a parent

explanation.surface: A mother keeping quiet can still be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apparent is plainly visible or evident.

clue.text: Wholesalers of engine parts

definitions.meaning: traders who supply goods to shops
devices in a petrol engine sending current to each spark plug in turn

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both suppliers handing goods on to retailers and the ignition component sharing out current to the plugs.

clue.text: Got up for a lady

definitions.meaning: ... from bed or a seat, past tense
a woman's given name, also a flower given to a lady

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of getting up and a common female first name.

clue.text: Nobody kept such a record

parts.note: seems to say no one kept a log, but The ___ of a Nobody is the Grossmith brothers' comic novel of a clerk's daily journal

explanation.surface: No one bothered to keep a log of events.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diary of a Nobody (1892) by George and Weedon Grossmith is a classic English comic novel; Nobody is a person here.
explanation.definitionFit: A daily personal journal is the kind of record kept by Charles Pooter, the Nobody of the novel.

clue.text: Sportsman's down to squander

definitions.meaning: an Oxford or Cambridge athlete who has represented the university
to blow or waste money recklessly

explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a Blue is someone who has played for the university against the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers an Oxbridge sporting award holder, a gloomy mood and wasting money.

clue.text: Blake's symmetrical night, burner

parts.note: William Blake's poem has a beast burning bright in the forests of the night with fearful symmetry

explanation.surface: A fragment describing a poet's balanced, glowing night.
explanation.walkthrough: Blake's poem 'The Tyger' opens 'burning bright, in the forests of the night' and asks who could frame its 'fearful symmetry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake's poem portrays the big striped cat as burning bright with fearful symmetry.

clue.text: What size of plug is needed for temptresses?

definitions.text: What size of plug is needed for temptresses?

parts.words: What size of plug is needed for temptresses?
parts.note: plugs are rated by current, so the size reads as a number of units of current, with a V in front; seductive women are the real sense

explanation.surface: An electrician asks what rating of plug some seductive women need.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamps are seductive women who use their charms to exploit men.

clue.text: Reproduction is Titian we hear from one who knows about figures

parts.note: a stat is short for a photostat, a photographic copy

indicators.note: we hear says the painter's name is taken by its sound only

parts.note: the Venetian painter, whose name is pronounced tish-un

explanation.surface: A copy of a painting is said to be a genuine Titian, according to an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: A statistician is an expert in numerical data.

clue.text: Bill presented to junior minister? Quite correct!

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a curate is an assistant member of the clergy, a junior church minister

explanation.surface: Handing the bill to a junior government minister is quite right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' suggests government; here the minister is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means exactly right, without error.

clue.text: No room underneath the arches for Bobby!

definitions.text: No room underneath the arches for Bobby!

parts.words: No room underneath the arches for Bobby!
parts.note: suggests a homeless person under a railway bridge, but fallen arches leave the sole level, and that slang is a name for a policeman

explanation.surface: A homeless man called Bobby finds no space beneath the railway arches.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is a British policeman; 'under the arches' was where the homeless slept.
explanation.definitionFit: This slang word for a police officer, especially a beat officer, comes from feet with fallen arches.

clue.text: I reclaim spot for development somewhere like Spain

indicators.note: development suggests the letters are built into something new

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: A developer plans to reclaim a site somewhere sunny.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's warm climate is near-tropical, bordering the subtropics.

clue.text: Embarrassed coming out of purdah?

indicators.note: coming out of suggests the letters emerge in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: A woman leaving seclusion feels self-conscious.
explanation.walkthrough: Embarrassed here means financially short, not blushing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being financially embarrassed is being short of money.

clue.text: Agitation obvious in centre, more probably

indicators.note: in says the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Unrest is plain in the middle, and probably more.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a trembling or shaking, a state of nervous agitation.

clue.text: Describing non-smoking compartment of first-class lines

parts.note: A1 is first-class, written as letters A and I
RY is short for railway lines

explanation.surface: A note on a no-smoking carriage of a first-class train.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-smoking compartment would be fresh and well ventilated.

clue.text: Murphy, for example, to drive back in reverse

indicators.note: in reverse says the word for drive back is read from its end

parts.note: to rebut is to repel or drive back

explanation.surface: Someone called Murphy is told to back the car up.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is slang for a potato, from the Irish surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is the swollen underground stem of the plant.

clue.text: Play on words takes time in a boat

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: Someone takes time over a joke while out in a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A punt is a flat-bottomed boat pushed with a pole on English rivers.

clue.text: At home, cheer-leaders move by degrees

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: leaders points to the opening letters of the word cheer

explanation.surface: Cheerleaders in their own stadium edge forward slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: To inch is to move along very slowly, a little at a time.

clue.text: Music maker whose notes don't sound true!

definitions.text: Music maker whose notes don't sound true!

parts.words: Music maker whose notes don't sound true!
parts.note: an out-of-tune musician is suggested, but the instrument's name sounds like a teller of untruths

explanation.surface: An instrument player keeps hitting false notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyre is an ancient stringed instrument, whose name is said like a word for one who tells falsehoods.

clue.text: Colony's party favourite

parts.note: a do is a party
a minion was a favourite of a king or patron

explanation.surface: A colony throws a party for its favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominion was a self-governing colony in the British Empire.

clue.text: Energetic sort has Monday off

indicators.note: off says the letters of the day are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: A lively person takes Monday off work.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a very energetic, forceful person.

clue.text: Unbalanced chap sure to buy something

indicators.note: unbalanced suggests the letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unstable man is sure he will buy something.
explanation.definitionFit: To purchase is to buy, acquiring goods for money.

clue.text: Fleet Street area in slight depression, yet gracious

indicators.note: in places the postal area inside the depression

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow
EC is the East Central London postal district containing Fleet Street

explanation.surface: Fleet Street is in a slight slump, yet remains gracious.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street, the old home of British newspapers, lies in London's EC postcode area.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent here means kind and obliging, as in a decent gesture.
